items.text: Sums make sense in $E=\operatorname{Top}(X)$: decompositions of an object, connected objects.
X\ \text{connected non-empty}\iff \pi_0(X)=\mathrm{pt}
X\neq\varnothing\iff (\varnothing\to e)\ \text{is not an isomorphism}
$X=\varnothing\iff E\simeq$ the one-point category.
Cohomology from $E$
$E_{ab}$ = abelian group objects of $E$: enough injectives. SGA 4, exposé V.
\Gamma(F)=\operatorname{Hom}_E(e,F)=F(X)\qquad\text{left exact}
Not right exact (epi does not give onto on global sections): derive it.
H^i(X,F)=R^i\Gamma(F)
H^i(X,M)=H^i(X,M_X)\qquad M_X\ \text{constant sheaf}
X\ \text{connected}\iff \mathbf Z\to H^0(X,\mathbf Z)\ \text{surjective}
$H^0(X,\mathbf Z)$ = locally constant maps $X\to\mathbf Z$ (sections of $X\times I\to X$, $I$ discrete).
X\ \text{connected, non-empty}\iff \mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X,\mathbf Z)
Simply connected is not just $H^1=0$: more care.
Homotopy from $E$
Čech method (Artin–Mazur, étale homotopy types, Springer LNM): coverings and nerves.
The lattice of open sets = the lattice of subobjects of $e$: recovered from $E$.
Fundamental group and coverings
Coverings of $X$ $\leftrightarrow$ sets with an action of $\pi_1(X,x)$ ($X$ connected, locally simply connected).
A covering is locally constant: $X'$ étale and
e=\sup_i U_i,\qquad X'\times_e U_i\ \simeq\ \coprod_{S_i}U_i
Locally constant objects of $E$: defined in any category with sums.
If $X$ is not locally simply connected: a pro-group classifies the coverings.
Non-commutative cohomology
$G$ a sheaf of non-commutative groups: $H^1(X,G)$ and a little $H^2(X,G)$.
H^1(X,G)=\{\text{torsors under } G\}/\text{isomorphism}
G\times P\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }P\times P,\qquad P\twoheadrightarrow e
$G$ an ordinary group: $H^1(X,G)=H^1(X,G_X)$, $G_X=\coprod_G e$ (left exact).
Torsors under $G_X$ = Galois coverings with group $G$.
H^1(X,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1,G)/\text{inner automorphisms}
$X$ simply connected iff all these $H^1$ vanish.
Stacks and $H^2$
Fibred category over $\mathcal O$: for each open $U$ a category $F_U$; for $V\subset U$ a restriction functor $F_U\to F_V$.
Transitivity only up to given isomorphism (with axioms).
Examples: sheaves over $U$; fibre spaces; sheaves of groups; torsors under $G|_U$.
Local on morphisms: $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F,G)$ is a sheaf.
V\mapsto \operatorname{Hom}(F|_V,G|_V)\ \text{a sheaf on } U
Local on objects: objects over the $U_i$, isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}$ on $U_{ij}$, and a cocycle condition on $U_{ijk}$.
\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}\quad\text{on } U_{ijk}
Both conditions: a stack. Thousands of examples (local/global games).
$H^2(X,G)$ = classes of stacks attached to $G$. Reference: Giraud (Grundlehren); résumé published at Columbia.
Needs only the lattice of opens, so $H^2$ also depends only on $E$.
In a general topos the final object may have few subobjects: use all objects.
For $X'$ étale over $X$, covered by opens $U'_i\hookrightarrow X$:
F_{X'}=\{(x_i\in F_{U'_i}),\ \text{isomorphisms on } U'_{ij},\ \text{cocycle}\}
Fibred category over $E$; coverings = epimorphic families $X'_i\to X'$, intersections = fibre products over $X'$.
Stacks on $\mathcal O$ $\simeq$ stacks on $E$: restriction and extension are inverse.
More dictionary entries
Local connectedness, compactness, total disconnectedness are expressible in $E$.
Maps: $f^*$ determines $f_*$ (adjoint). $f$ dominant ($f(X)$ dense) iff $f^*$ faithful. SGA 4 full of such exercises.
\operatorname{Top}(X\sqcup Y)\simeq\operatorname{Top}(X)\times\operatorname{Top}(Y)\qquad\operatorname{Top}\bigl(\textstyle\coprod X_i\bigr)\simeq\prod\operatorname{Top}(X_i)
Sum of spaces = product of categories.
Gluing: $Z$ closed in $X$ and in $Y$; $X\cup_Z Y$ (e.g. two lines glued at a point).
\begin{CD} \operatorname{Top}(X\cup_Z Y) @>>> \operatorname{Top}(X)\\ @VVV @VVV\\ \operatorname{Top}(Y) @>>> \operatorname{Top}(Z) \end{CD}
2-cartesian: a sheaf on the glued space = sheaves on $X$, $Y$ and an isomorphism of their restrictions to $Z$.
Wild quotients $X/R$: pathological as spaces, but the topos defined by such a diagram is useful: a generalised space.
Recovering the space
Preliminaries. $Z$ is irreducible if $Z\neq\varnothing$ and
Z=Z_1\cup Z_2\ \text{closed}\ \Longrightarrow\ Z_1=Z\ \text{or}\ Z_2=Z
A Hausdorff space is irreducible iff it is a point. Zariski topology: the usual notion.
$T$ irreducible $\Rightarrow$ $\overline T$ irreducible.
i\colon X\to\tilde X,\quad x\mapsto\overline{\{x\}},\qquad \tilde X=\{\text{irreducible closed subsets of } X\}
$X$ Hausdorff: $i$ bijective. For spectra of rings: most points not closed.
Topology on $\tilde X$: for $U$ open in $X$,
\tilde U=\{Y\in\tilde X:\ Y\cap U\neq\varnothing\}\ \longleftrightarrow\ \{\text{irreducible closed subsets of } U\}
\widetilde{\textstyle\bigcup_i U_i}=\bigcup_i\tilde U_i,\qquad \widetilde{U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_n}=\bigcap_i\tilde U_i
Intersection of non-empty opens of an irreducible space is non-empty.
i^{-1}(\tilde U)=U
$x\in U\iff\overline{\{x\}}\cap U\ne\varnothing$. So $i$ is continuous and induces an isomorphism of lattices of open sets.
Hence $\operatorname{Top}(\tilde X)\to\operatorname{Top}(X)$ is an isomorphism of categories, not just an equivalence.
